C006.subject: Intermittent fasting
C006.predicate: is more effective than continuous calorie restriction for
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Intermittent fasting short-term weight loss (≤12 months)]

[PATH:empirical] Randomized controlled trial comparing time-restricted eating (16:8) vs. daily calorie restriction over 12 months, with equal caloric deficits prescribed in both arms. — Direct head-to-head comparison under controlled conditions would isolate the effect of intermittent fasting schedule from total calorie intake, addressing the core dispute about relative efficacy for short-term weight loss.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of all RCTs (≥6 months duration) comparing intermittent fasting protocols to continuous calorie restriction, with subgroup analysis by study quality and adherence rates. — Synthesizing existing evidence can increase statistical power to detect differences, and adherence analysis would clarify whether any observed advantage is due to the fasting schedule itself or better compliance.

[PATH:theoretical] Mechanistic study examining differences in metabolic adaptation, gut microbiome composition, and circadian gene expression between intermittent fasting and continuous restriction over 12 weeks. — Understanding underlying biological pathways (e.g., hormonal responses, energy expenditure) could explain or predict differential weight loss outcomes, providing a theoretical basis to confirm or refute the hypothesis beyond mere observational data.

C007.subject: Long-term adherence to intermittent fasting

[PATH:empirical] Randomized controlled trial comparing 12-month adherence rates between intermittent fasting (e.g., 5:2 or time-restricted eating) and continuous calorie restriction in adults with high baseline dietary restraint, with validated measures of dropout and dietary lapses. — Directly tests the hypothesis in the specified scope (adherence beyond 12 months, high dietary restraint) and can confirm or refute whether high restraint paradoxically increases dropout from intermittent fasting.

[PATH:empirical] Longitudinal observational study using ecological momentary assessment to track perceived deprivation, binge triggers, and adherence in individuals with high dietary restraint who initiate intermittent fasting versus continuous calorie restriction over 12+ months. — Provides mechanistic evidence for the qualifier note: whether high restraint leads to greater perceived deprivation and binge triggers in intermittent fasting, which would mediate lower adherence.

[PATH:literature] Systematic review and meta-analysis of adherence rates in dietary interventions, stratified by baseline dietary restraint scores, comparing intermittent fasting and continuous calorie restriction outcomes beyond 12 months. — Synthesizes existing data to assess whether the pattern holds across studies, addressing the disputed status and providing higher-level evidence for the hypothesis.
